title: Beyond the 956: Cedrick Cunningham, 50, Charged With Murder After Alleged Fatal Stabbing at Prison-Release Party in South Carolina
excerpt: Cedrick Cunningham, 50, was charged with murder after allegedly stabbing 42-year-old Andre Smith to death at a gathering in Hopkins, South Carolina, celebrating Cunningham's release from federal prison.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A South Carolina man was charged with murder after he allegedly stabbed another man to death at a gathering celebrating his own release from federal prison, authorities said.

Cedrick Cunningham, 50, was charged Monday with murder and possession of a weapon during a violent crime in connection with the death of 42-year-old Andre Smith, according to the Richland County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies found Smith dead inside a car on Saturday in Hopkins, South Carolina, with a large laceration on his chest, WIS News 10 reported. The Richland County Coroner's Office identified him as Andre J. Smith, 42, of Eastover.

According to authorities, Cunningham was at a celebration held after his release from federal prison when he and Smith, who knew each other, got into an altercation. Investigators allege the confrontation escalated and Cunningham stabbed Smith.

Federal records show Cunningham was sentenced to 10 years in prison in 2019 after pleading guilty to a weapons charge. A judge denied his request for compassionate release in 2023, and details of his release status were not immediately clear. A search of the Federal Bureau of Prisons website listed Cunningham at a Residential Reentry Management office in Raleigh, North Carolina, and WIS said it has asked the bureau for more details.

Richland County Sheriff Leon Lott announced the arrest on Tuesday. Cunningham was being held at the Alvin S. Glenn Detention Center as of Tuesday. Authorities have not said what led to the altercation, and the investigation remains ongoing.

Cunningham is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) Instagram post, Nov. 18, 2026; WIS News 10 / Gray News via WVLT, Nov. 18, 2026; International Business Times, Nov. 18, 2026.
